label: Scene Story
line: Put a person, named only by role, inside an act already under way. Turn it with 'but when' inside the first fifth, hold the reveal to the last quarter, and stop on a hard fact.
best_for: one person inside one moment: a near miss, a strange true incident, an ordinary life in a big event
a fact that can ride on a story as the answer to its question
also_for: the rise or fall of a product, told through one decision
avoid_for: a biography or a survey of a period

beats.name: The act
beats.job: A pronoun or a role, in the middle of doing something. No name and no date with a life history.

beats.name: Escalation
beats.job: Remove the ways out. Plant one detail for later.

beats.name: Reveal
beats.job: As a plain noun or a look back: bigger than the threat the viewer knew about.

beats.name: Last line
beats.job: A hard fact, an ironic clause or a what-if. Never a moral.

hooks.shape: In [year], [a person, by role] was [doing X] in [a cut-off place] when [the sudden failure].
This is [a harmless-looking thing], and it [did something that should be impossible].
By [the next morning], [the outcome]. It began with [one small act].

holds: The viewer knows only what the person in the scene knows. One or two 'but' turns in every thirty seconds. One line that withholds, a beat before the reveal: they could not believe what they saw.
ending: A reveal of a few words, an ironic last clause or a what-if. The script stops on the payoff detail and asks nothing.
pitfalls: A name and a date before any reason to care
The outcome in the title or the first line (unless the opening is the result-first shape)
template: [A person, by role] was [in the middle of an act]. But when [the first turn], [reaction]. [A constraint]. [The planted detail]. Now, [time marker], [it kept happening]. So [a decision]. When [they] looked, [they] could not believe it. It was [the reveal]. [A hard fact or an ironic clause].
